finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST /hooks/test route on the public router sends a server-side HTTP POST to a user-supplied callback URL with no validation. The response only exposes the status code, so this is semi-blind SSRF. It still allows internal port and host scanning, hitting internal POST endpoints, and reaching cloud metadata services.
finding.source: req.body.callback (any remote client, POST body of /hooks/test)

trace.note: pub router is created with no auth middleware
upstream status code is returned to the caller, giving an oracle for reachability

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or allowlist check, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no DNS-rebinding protection. requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router (routes.js:12), not to pub. axios follows redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass is also possible. Any app-level auth mounted outside this file could not be seen; only routes.js exists.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post on the `pub` router (routes.js:4, 19), which has no auth middleware (requireAdmin at routes.js:12 covers only `admin`), and routes.js:21 returns the upstream status; no URL validation exists, though app-level auth outside this file can't be ruled out since routes.js is the only file.

finding.claim: SSRF in the admin diagnostics fetch endpoint: GET /diagnostics/fetch issues a server-side GET to an arbitrary URL taken from the query string. It is restricted to admin sessions, so exploitation needs an admin account or session compromise (for example XSS or CSRF against an admin). Only the status code is returned.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates the router on session role

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin checks req.session.role === 'admin' (routes.js:7-10), which limits the attack surface. There is no URL scheme, host or IP validation and no internal-address blocking. This is lower severity than finding 1 because of the admin gate. The GET route has no CSRF protection visible here.

verdict.guard_found: none on the URL; the admin-role gate requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) restricts who can reach the sink
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16), but the URL at routes.js:15 can only be supplied by a session with role "admin" (routes.js:8, 12), so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. The CSRF/XSS route to an admin session is speculative and is not shown in this code.
